// five systems

What's actually running

Each piece is independently real — built, tested, and verified on its own, then wired together.

01data

Data Platform

Incremental, idempotent ingestion from the NYC 311 API into Cloud Storage, then a partitioned, clustered BigQuery warehouse. Retry with exponential backoff; state tracked so a crash never duplicates data.

PythonGCSBigQuery
Verified: reran ingestion twice — zero duplicate rows
02orchestration

Transformation & Orchestration

dbt models compute SLA-breach risk using a 90th-percentile threshold per complaint type — not a guessed number. Airflow runs the full five-step pipeline daily, fully containerized.

dbtAirflowDocker
Verified: 8/8 dbt tests passing, all 5 Airflow tasks green
03streaming

Real-Time Pipeline

A Kafka/Redpanda producer streams high-priority complaints — water, gas, heat, structural — the moment they're ingested, independent of the daily batch schedule.

KafkaRedpanda
Verified: 84/84 priority events produced and consumed correctly
04ai

AI Operations Assistant

A LangGraph agent turns plain-English questions into SQL against the live warehouse — independently validated before it ever runs, with a self-correcting retry loop and multi-turn memory.

LangGraphOllama / Llama 3.1Guardrails
Verified: adversarial testing found and closed a real validator gap
05ml

ML & Analytics

A Random Forest model predicts SLA-breach risk before a complaint is resolved, trained only on features available at creation time — no data leakage, evaluated without cherry-picking.

Scikit-learnpandas
Verified: honest precision/recall reported, not hidden

// model evaluation

The ML model, evaluated honestly

No inflated accuracy number. Here's exactly what it catches, what it gets wrong, and why.

64%
breach recall
15%
breach precision
9.4%
real-world base breach rate
26,863
training records
HONEST FINDING
Threshold tuning was tested across six cutoffs (0.2–0.7) and produced a sharp precision/recall "cliff" rather than a smooth tradeoff — proof the model isn't confidently separating outcomes yet. Conclusion: the bottleneck is feature quality, not calibration. Documented, not hidden, with concrete next steps in the repo.

// incident log

Real bugs, found and closed

Every system here was tested adversarially, not just for the happy path.

postmortems2 resolved
RESOLVED
SQL validator allowed an unbounded query to slip through on retry
Adversarial test ("delete all noise complaints from the Bronx") was correctly blocked, but the automatic retry generated a SELECT with no LIMIT and no aggregate — the validator's exemption logic wrongly assumed that shape couldn't happen. Fix: now requires a LIMIT unless every selected column is a genuine aggregate. Regression test added permanently.
RESOLVED
BigQuery load script duplicated 25,000 rows into 50,000
The load step had no record of which files were already loaded, so a rerun reloaded everything. Fix: added a state file tracking loaded files, matching the same idempotency pattern already used in ingestion. Cleanup script written to repair the affected table.
